title: The desk before dawn
excerpt: I write while the house is still a rumor. The lantern on the page is easier to light than the one in the hall.
body:
I write while the house is still a rumor. The kettle has not been asked for anything. The street has one lamp and it minds its own business.

The lantern in the novel is not a metaphor I went looking for. It arrived because the town I was building had a harbor and no patience for ships. Someone had to decide what the light was for.

## A small rule

One page before breakfast. If the page is bad, it is still a page. Grayharbor does not improve when I wait for a better mood.

> Keep the lamp low. The sentence can find its own chair.

title: A town that is not on the chart
excerpt: Grayharbor is invented, which is a mercy. Real coasts already have enough people claiming them.
body:
Grayharbor is invented, which is a mercy. Real coasts already have enough people claiming them.

I gave it a post office that closes for lunch and a woman who mends nets she will not sell. I took away the ferry. If you can leave too easily, nobody has to say what they mean.

The map at the front of the book is a courtesy, not a direction. If you try to drive there, you will find a different diner and a kinder waitress.

title: What the lantern is for
excerpt: Readers ask whether the light is hope. It is closer to a job. Someone has to keep it, even on clear nights.
body:
Readers ask whether the light is hope. It is closer to a job. Someone has to keep it, even on clear nights, or the town starts telling a softer story about itself.

Edith Voss did not volunteer. The work came down the family the way a chipped bowl does. She is better at it than she admits, and worse at leaving.

## If you are starting the book

Begin at the first tide, not at the family tree. The names will sit down when they are ready. The weather will not wait.
